ap_computer_science_a-f01.title: PasswordCheck: counting uppercase letters and rating a password

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Write the method countUpper, which returns the number of uppercase letters (A through Z) in the String s. For example, countUpper("Hello World") returns 2 and countUpper("abc") returns 0. Complete the method countUpper.

rubric_rows.criterion: Iterates over every character of s with a loop whose bounds are correct (first through last index)
Tests each character for being between A and Z inclusive (or an equivalent test)
Increments (or otherwise accumulates) a counter only for uppercase characters
Initializes the counter before the loop and returns it after the loop

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Write the method rate, which returns a String that rates the strength of the password s. The rating is "strong" if s has at least 6 characters and at least 2 uppercase letters; otherwise "medium" if s has at least 6 characters or at least 1 uppercase letter; otherwise "weak". Your solution must call countUpper from part (a). Assume that countUpper works as specified.

rubric_rows.criterion: Calls countUpper(s) and uses its result (does not duplicate the counting loop)
Compares s.length() with 6 using a correct boundary (at least 6)
Returns "strong" exactly when the length condition and the uppercase count of at least 2 both hold
Returns "medium" exactly when the length condition or at least one uppercase letter holds (and the password is not strong)
Returns "weak" otherwise; the tests are ordered or combined so exactly one value is returned for every input

ap_computer_science_a-f02.title: StepTracker: design a class

parts.label: a
parts.prompt:
Write the complete StepTracker class, including the constructor and any required instance variables and methods. A StepTracker records the number of steps taken on each day. The constructor takes the minimum number of steps for a day to count as active. addDailySteps records one more day. activeDays returns the number of recorded days with at least the minimum number of steps. averageSteps returns the average number of steps per recorded day as a double, or 0.0 if no days have been recorded. Examples of the behavior are listed in the following table.

| Statement | Value returned | Explanation |
|---|---|---|
| StepTracker t = new StepTracker(5000); | (none) | A tracker whose active-day minimum is 5000 steps |
| t.addDailySteps(5500); | (none) | One day with 5500 steps |
| t.addDailySteps(3000); | (none) | A second day, below the minimum |
| t.activeDays() | 1 | Only the first day counted as active |
| t.averageSteps() | 4250.0 | The mean of the two days |

rubric_rows.criterion: Declares the class header public class StepTracker
common_errors: declares an interface or a method named StepTracker

rubric_rows.criterion: Declares private instance variables sufficient to store the minimum and the data needed by all methods
common_errors: declares the variables inside a method

rubric_rows.criterion: Declares a public constructor with one int parameter that stores the minimum in an instance variable
common_errors: assigns the parameter to itself without this

rubric_rows.criterion: addDailySteps updates the stored data to reflect one more day (steps are accumulated, not replaced)
addDailySteps (or activeDays) counts a day as active exactly when steps is at least the minimum
activeDays returns the number of active days (declared int, public)
averageSteps handles the case of no recorded days by returning 0.0 without dividing by zero
averageSteps computes the average using floating-point division (a cast or double operand)
All methods have the correct headers and return types (void, int, double) and the class compiles as a whole

ap_computer_science_a-f02.reference_note: ALTON reference answer for self-review — not official AP scoring

ap_computer_science_a-f03.title: DataTools: values above the average of an ArrayList

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Write the method aboveAverage, which returns a new ArrayList<Integer> containing the values of data that are strictly greater than the average of all the values in data, in their original order. The method must not modify data and returns an empty list when data is empty. For example, if data is [1, 2, 3, 10] the average is 4.0 and the method returns [10]. Complete the method aboveAverage.

rubric_rows.criterion: Creates a new ArrayList<Integer> to hold the result and returns it (the original list is not returned or modified)
Handles an empty list without an exception (empty result, no division by zero)
Traverses all of data to accumulate the sum using get(i) or an enhanced for loop with correct bounds
Computes the average of all values (not of a subset) and does not lose the fractional part
Makes a second pass (or an equivalent single approach) that examines every element again after the average is known
Tests each element for being strictly greater than the average
Adds qualifying elements to the result
Preserves the original order of the qualifying elements
Does not remove elements from data while it is traversed and the code compiles with correct ArrayList and Integer use
